Using the ACRA “Information on Corporate Entities” datasets and SSIC 2020 classifications, we select at least **three business types** (2- or 3-digit SSIC) and analyse how their locations and intensities evolve over time. Our workflow mirrors the point-pattern framework taught in class: - **Data wrangling & geocoding:** tidy ACRA records, standardise dates/SSIC codes, and geocode by postal code via OneMap; convert to `sf` with SVY21 (EPSG:3414). - **Exploratory mapping:** counts by subzone/planning area to establish baseline patterns. - **First-order analysis (intensity):** **Kernel Density Estimation (KDE)** to reveal spatial hot spots for each SSIC and period. - **Second-order analysis (dependence):** **Ripley’s K / CSR envelopes** to test whether registrations are clustered, random, or dispersed. - **Spatio-temporal analysis:** **STKDE** (monthly slices) to detect **emerging, persistent, and fading** clusters over the study window. The results are communicated through cartographic maps and concise figure captions words , followed by a synthesis translating findings into **urban land-use and economic development implications**—e.g., infrastructure readiness, zoning flexibility, activation of under-served subzones, and monitoring of over-concentration risks. ## The Data This study uses ACRA corporate entity registrations combined with reference layers and services to enable spatial and spatio-temporal analysis. ### Data sources | Dataset Name | Description | Format | Provider | Notes | |---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------| | **ACRA – Information on Corporate Entities (A–Z, Others)** | All entity registrations. Used to extract new businesses by SSIC and date. | CSV (27 files) | data.gov.sg / ACRA | Split alphabetically: A–Z plus a 27th file for names starting with digits/symbols. | | **SSIC 2020** | Singapore Standard Industrial Classification; used to choose business types (2-/3-/5-digit). | CSV/XLSX | SingStat | We derive `ssic2`, `ssic3` and use `primary_ssic_code`. | | **OneMap Search API** | Geocoding service to convert postal codes to coordinates. | Web API | SLA / OneMap | Returns WGS84 (lat/lon). We transform to SVY21 (EPSG:3414). | | **Master Plan Subzones (MPSZ 2024)** | Administrative subzone polygons for aggregation and mapping. | GPKG/Shapefile | data.gov.sg / URA/SLA | Reprojected to SVY21 (EPSG:3414) for analysis. | ### Fields used (ACRA) | Field | Meaning | Example | |------------------------|------------------------|------------------------| | `uen` | Unique Entity Number (entity identifier) | 201912345K | | `entity_name` | Registered business name | ABC PTE. LTD. | | `registration_incorporation_date` | Registration date (YYYY-MM-DD) | 2025-03-14 | | `primary_ssic_code` | Primary SSIC code (2/3/4/5-digit) | 56111 | | `postal_code` | Registered postal code (should be 6 digits) | 018989 | | `entity_type` / `status` | Type/status if required for filtering | LIVE COMPANY | > Additional columns may exist in different ACRA dumps; we standardise names with `janitor::clean_names()` and coalesce equivalent fields where needed. ### Study coverage - **Temporal window:** 1 Jan 2024 – 30 Jun 2025 (inclusive).\ - **Spatial extent:** Singapore national boundary; mapping/aggregation by **subzone** and **planning area**.\ - **Business scope:** At least **three** SSIC types (2- or 3-digit groups, or 5-digit subclasses), selected prior to analysis. ### Pre-processing & wrangling (summary) - Read and row-bind **all 27 ACRA CSVs**; add `source_file` for provenance.\ - Standardise fields: parse `registration_incorporation_date` as Date (UTC), derive `year`, `month`.\ - **Postal code hygiene:** keep digits only, left-pad to 6; drop non-6-digit values before geocoding.\ - **Deduplicate** by `uen` + `registration_incorporation_date` (if necessary).\ - Filter to the target SSIC code set and to the study window.\ - **Geocode** unique postal codes via OneMap; join `X`/`Y` back to ACRA records.\ - Convert to `sf` (WGS84) → transform to **SVY21 (EPSG:3414)** for distance-based methods.\ - Join subzone attributes; save intermediates as RDS for reproducibility. ### Data quality & limitations - **Geocoding precision:** Postal codes resolve to building/entrance centroids, not unit-level; some industrial sites share codes.\ - **Registration vs. operation:** Registration date ≠ opening date; counts reflect legal registrations.\ - **Address anomalies:** Legacy/PO box or malformed postcodes may not geocode; these are excluded.\ - **Classification drift:** SSIC codes can change over time; we use the recorded `primary_ssic_code` as-is. ### Coordinate reference systems (CRS) - **Input:** WGS84 (EPSG:4326) from OneMap.\ - **Analysis/Maps:** SVY21 / Singapore TM (EPSG:3414), metres, suitable for KDE and K-functions. ### Ethical/usage notes - ACRA data contains **entity names** (public corporate info), not personal data.\ - Results are aggregated for planning insights; avoid singling out individual firms. ## Load Packages Following code chunk is used to load neccessary packages ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pacman::p_load(stpp, tidyverse, # dplyr/readr/purrr/stringr sf, tmap, # geospatial + mapping httr, # OneMap API calls lubridate, # year(), month(), etc. spatstat, spatstat.geom, spatstat.explore, # KDE, K-function, CSR (monolithic ok) spNetwork, # network KDE (optional/bonus) sparr, # relative risk (optional/bonus) plotly, # interactive plots (optional) gtsummary, # summary tables dplyr, janitor, stringr, readr, purrr ) ``` ::: ## Data Wrangling ### Preparing the Subzone Boundary (why & how) This chunk converts URA’s **Master Plan Subzone (No Sea)** GeoJSON into a clean, projected **GeoPackage** with consistent field names. We use it as: 1) the **analysis window** for point-pattern methods, and\ 2) the **join layer** to aggregate new businesses by subzone/planning area. Extract data for planning ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sz_raw_path <- "data/geospatial/MasterPlan2019SubzoneBoundaryNoSeaGEOJSON.geojson" subzones <- st_read(sz_raw_path, quiet = TRUE) %>% clean_names() %>% # lower_case_names st_make_valid() %>% # fix any tiny geometry issues st_transform(3414) # SVY21 metres (needed for KDE/K-functions) ``` ::: Standardise key attribute names ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Helper: extract a field value from the HTML in `description` extract_field <- function(html, key){ m <- str_match(html, paste0("", key, "\\s*([^<]*)")) val <- m[, 2] val <- ifelse(is.na(val) | val == "", NA_character_, str_squish(val)) return(val) } subzones_std <- subzones %>% mutate( SUBZONE_NO = as.integer(extract_field(description, "SUBZONE_NO")), SUBZONE_N = extract_field(description, "SUBZONE_N"), SUBZONE_C = extract_field(description, "SUBZONE_C"), CA_IND = extract_field(description, "CA_IND"), PLN_AREA_N = extract_field(description, "PLN_AREA_N"), PLN_AREA_C = extract_field(description, "PLN_AREA_C"), REGION_N = extract_field(description, "REGION_N"), REGION_C = extract_field(description, "REGION_C"), FMEL_UPD_D = extract_field(description, "FMEL_UPD_D") ) %>% select(SUBZONE_NO, SUBZONE_N, SUBZONE_C, CA_IND, PLN_AREA_N, PLN_AREA_C, REGION_N, REGION_C, FMEL_UPD_D, geometry) %>% st_make_valid() %>% st_transform(3414) # save a clean, fast-to-load copy st_write(subzones_std, "data/geospatial/mpsz_subzones_2019_nosea.gpkg", layer = "subzones", delete_dsn = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Deleting source `data/geospatial/mpsz_subzones_2019_nosea.gpkg' using driver `GPKG' Writing layer `subzones' to data source `data/geospatial/mpsz_subzones_2019_nosea.gpkg' using driver `GPKG' Writing 332 features with 9 fields and geometry type Unknown (any). ``` ::: ::: ### Load & Tidy Acra ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} aspatial_dir <- "data/aspatial" rds_dir <- "data/rds" dir.create(rds_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE) file_list <- list.files(aspatial_dir, pattern = "^ACRA.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE) acra_raw <- file_list |> map_dfr(~ read_csv(.x, show_col_types = FALSE)) |> clean_names() # 2) Tidy dates, SSIC, postal codes; derive time fields; filter study window acra_tidy <- acra_raw |> mutate( reg_date = as.Date(registration_incorporation_date), year = year(reg_date), month_num = month(reg_date), month = month(reg_date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE), # keep only digits in postal_code; left-pad to 6 postal_code = postal_code |> str_replace_all("[^0-9]", "") |> str_pad(width = 6, side = "left", pad = "0"), # normalise primary SSIC to 5 chars, and derive 2-/3-digit prefixes primary_ssic_code = str_pad(str_sub(primary_ssic_code, 1, 5), 5, pad = "0"), ssic2 = str_sub(primary_ssic_code, 1, 2), ssic3 = str_sub(primary_ssic_code, 1, 3) ) |> filter(!is.na(reg_date), reg_date >= as.Date("2024-01-01"), reg_date <= as.Date("2025-06-30")) ``` ::: ### Select the 3 Industries Choosing the three industries The assignment requires at least three business types. We select broad, policy-relevant **2-digit SSIC** groups that span consumer, knowledge, and logistics activities: - **56 — Food & Beverage Service Activities** (restaurants, cafés, bars)\ - **62 — Computer programming, IT consultancy & related activities**\ - **52 — Warehousing & support activities for transportation** In the code below, we: 1. **Build** a small lookup to attach readable sector labels to each 2-digit SSIC.\ 2. **Filter** the cleaned ACRA records to these codes.\ 3. **Produce** a quick *sector × year* table to sanity-check sample sizes for 2024 and 2025. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # 56 = Food & Beverage, 62 = Information Technology, 52 = Warehousing & support activities for transport targets <- tibble( ssic2 = c("56", "62", "52"), sector = c("F&B (56)", "IT (62)", "Logistics/Warehousing (52)") ) biz_sel <- acra_tidy |> filter(ssic2 %in% targets$ssic2) |> left_join(targets, by = "ssic2") table(biz_sel$sector, biz_sel$year) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 2024 2025 F&B (56) 3793 1965 IT (62) 5845 2895 Logistics/Warehousing (52) 995 723 ``` ::: ::: ### Geocode unique postcodes with OneMap ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Helper that hits OneMap Search API for one postcode onemap_lookup <- function(pc){ res <- GET("https://onemap.gov.sg/api/common/elastic/search", query = list(searchVal = pc, returnGeom = "Y", getAddrDetails = "Y", pageNum = "1")) js <- content(res) if (!is.null(js$found) && js$found > 0) { r <- js$results[[1]] tibble(POSTAL = r$POSTAL, X = as.numeric(r$X), Y = as.numeric(r$Y)) } else { tibble(POSTAL = pc, X = NA_real_, Y = NA_real_) } } # Geocode unique postcodes pcs <- biz_sel$postal_code |> unique() geo_tbl <- map_dfr(pcs, ~ tryCatch(onemap_lookup(.x), error = function(e) tibble(POSTAL = .x, X = NA_real_, Y = NA_real_))) # Join back and keep geocoded rows biz_geo <- biz_sel |> left_join(geo_tbl, by = c("postal_code" = "POSTAL")) |> filter(!is.na(X), !is.na(Y)) ``` ::: ### Convert to sf, project to SVY21, and join subzones ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} biz_pts <- st_as_sf(biz_geo, coords = c("X","Y"), crs = 4326) |> st_transform(3414) |> st_join(subzones_std |> dplyr::select(SUBZONE_N, PLN_AREA_N), left = TRUE) # Save intermediates for fast reload write_rds(acra_tidy, file.path(rds_dir, "acra_tidy_2024H1_2025H1.rds")) write_rds(biz_pts, file.path(rds_dir, "biz_points_geocoded.rds")) ``` ::: ### Load precomputed outputs ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} acra_tidy <- readr::read_rds(file.path(rds_dir, "acra_tidy_2024H1_2025H1.rds")) biz_pts <- readr::read_rds(file.path(rds_dir, "biz_points_geocoded.rds")) ``` ::: ### Quick sanity check #### counts, CRS, validity ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Expect these to exist from earlier chunks: stopifnot(exists("subzones_std"), exists("biz_pts")) # Basic shapes nrow(subzones_std); nrow(biz_pts) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 332 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 16213 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # CRS should be SVY21 / EPSG:3414 st_crs(subzones_std)$epsg ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3414 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} st_crs(biz_pts)$epsg ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3414 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Any invalid geometries? all(st_is_valid(subzones_std)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} all(st_is_valid(biz_pts)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Any missing coordinates? sum(is.na(st_coordinates(biz_pts)[,1])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} sum(is.na(st_coordinates(biz_pts)[,2])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Quick distribution check biz_pts |> st_drop_geometry() |> count(sector, year, name = "n") |> arrange(sector, year) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 3 sector year n 1 F&B (56) 2024 3791 2 F&B (56) 2025 1965 3 IT (62) 2024 5844 4 IT (62) 2025 2895 5 Logistics/Warehousing (52) 2024 995 6 Logistics/Warehousing (52) 2025 723 ``` ::: ::: #### Are points inside Singapore subzones? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} inside <- st_intersects(biz_pts, subzones_std, sparse = TRUE) mean(lengths(inside) > 0) # share of points that fall in a subzone (expect ~1) ``` ::: we find that intersects results in 0 which means some thing went wrong somewhere therefore we rectify this in the next Sub section #### Rebuild the sf points with the correct CRS directly (no transform) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # X/Y from OneMap are already SVY21 metres → set crs = 3414 and DO NOT transform biz_pts <- st_as_sf(biz_geo, coords = c("X","Y"), crs = 3414) |> st_join(subzones_std |> dplyr::select(SUBZONE_N, PLN_AREA_N), left = TRUE) # Quick sanity stopifnot(st_crs(biz_pts)$epsg == 3414) mean(lengths(st_intersects(biz_pts, subzones_std)) > 0) # should be ~1 # Overwrite the saved file write_rds(biz_pts, file.path(rds_dir, "biz_points_geocoded.rds")) ``` ::: #### Load precomputed outputs again ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} acra_tidy <- readr::read_rds(file.path(rds_dir, "acra_tidy_2024H1_2025H1.rds")) biz_pts <- readr::read_rds(file.path(rds_dir, "biz_points_geocoded.rds")) ``` ::: #### Quick Check again ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #| label: qc-rebuild-using-biz-pts #| eval: true # Coordinate ranges in SVY21 metres coords <- sf::st_coordinates(biz_pts) summary(coords) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` X Y Min. : 4721 Min. :24733 1st Qu.:28071 1st Qu.:29868 Median :29744 Median :33206 Mean :29492 Mean :34315 3rd Qu.:32938 3rd Qu.:36953 Max. :53137 Max. :50104 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Validity + missing checks all(sf::st_is_valid(biz_pts)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} sum(is.na(coords[,1])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} sum(is.na(coords[,2])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Coverage inside subzones inside <- sf::st_intersects(biz_pts, subzones_std, sparse = TRUE) mean(lengths(inside) > 0) # should be ~1 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1 ``` ::: ::: Now intersects() does leave 1 which means all points are in Singapore #### Quick Map ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tmap_mode("plot") tm_shape(subzones_std) + tm_polygons(col = "grey90", border.col = "white") + tm_shape(biz_pts) + tm_dots(size = 0.02, alpha = 0.5) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Take_Home_Ex01_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### Removing unwanted planning areas To avoid empty polygons biasing our maps and point-pattern statistics, we trim the study area to places that actually have registrations. Specifically, we: - **Keep** planning areas with ≥ 1 geocoded point (computed from `biz_pts`).\ - **Exclude** *NORTH-EASTERN ISLANDS* on purpose (offshore, no relevant activity for our scope).\ - **Keep** *WESTERN ISLANDS* because logistics/port activity is plausible.\ - **Filter** both the polygon layer (`subzones_std → subzones_use`) and the points (`biz_pts → biz_pts_use`) so subsequent joins and KDE/K-functions use a consistent window. This reduces noise, speeds processing, and prevents intensity estimates from being diluted by large empty areas. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Planning areas that have at least one point keep_pa <- biz_pts |> st_drop_geometry() |> count(PLN_AREA_N, name = "n") |> filter(n > 0) |> pull(PLN_AREA_N) subzones_use <- subzones_std |> filter(PLN_AREA_N %in% keep_pa) subzones_use <- subzones_std |> dplyr::filter(PLN_AREA_N %in% keep_pa, PLN_AREA_N != "NORTH-EASTERN ISLANDS") # also drop any biz points that lie in North-Eastern Islands, # or that didn’t pick up a planning area for any reason. biz_pts_use <- biz_pts |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(PLN_AREA_N), PLN_AREA_N != "NORTH-EASTERN ISLANDS") ``` ::: #### Map Check ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tmap_mode("plot") tm_shape(subzones_use) + tm_polygons(col = "grey90", border.col = "white") + tm_shape(biz_pts) + tm_dots(size = 0.02, alpha = 0.5) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Take_Home_Ex01_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## EDA ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Sector x Year counts biz_pts_use |> st_drop_geometry() |> count(sector, year, name = "n") |> arrange(sector, year) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 3 sector year n 1 F&B (56) 2024 3790 2 F&B (56) 2025 1965 3 IT (62) 2024 5844 4 IT (62) 2025 2895 5 Logistics/Warehousing (52) 2024 995 6 Logistics/Warehousing (52) 2025 723 ``` ::: ::: ### Top Planning Areas per sector ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Top Planning Areas per sector (top 10) top_pa <- biz_pts_use |> st_drop_geometry() |> count(sector, PLN_AREA_N, name = "n") |> group_by(sector) |> slice_max(n, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup() top_pa ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 30 × 3 sector PLN_AREA_N n 1 F&B (56) GEYLANG 526 2 F&B (56) DOWNTOWN CORE 362 3 F&B (56) KALLANG 294 4 F&B (56) WOODLANDS 287 5 F&B (56) OUTRAM 283 6 F&B (56) BEDOK 269 7 F&B (56) HOUGANG 254 8 F&B (56) SEMBAWANG 210 9 F&B (56) TOA PAYOH 210 10 F&B (56) YISHUN 209 # ℹ 20 more rows ``` ::: ::: ### Subzone coverage check: how many subzones have ≥1 registration (by sector) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # all sector × subzone combinations in your study window all_grid <- expand_grid( sector = unique(biz_pts_use$sector), SUBZONE_N = unique(subzones_use$SUBZONE_N) ) # fill missing combos with n = 0, then compute has_any subzone_cover <- biz_pts_use |> st_drop_geometry() |> count(sector, SUBZONE_N, name = "n") |> right_join(all_grid, by = c("sector","SUBZONE_N")) |> mutate(n = replace_na(n, 0), has_any = n > 0) |> count(sector, has_any, name = "subzones") |> tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = has_any, values_from = subzones, values_fill = 0) |> rename(`subzones_with_≥1` = `TRUE`, `subzones_with_0` = `FALSE`) |> mutate(subzones_total = `subzones_with_≥1` + `subzones_with_0`) |> select(sector, subzones_total, `subzones_with_≥1`, `subzones_with_0`) |> arrange(sector) subzone_cover ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 4 sector subzones_total `subzones_with_≥1` subzones_with_0 1 F&B (56) 319 278 41 2 IT (62) 319 260 59 3 Logistics/Warehousing (52) 319 202 117 ``` ::: ::: - **Headline:** IT and Logistics appear to “peak” in the CBD due to *registered-office addresses*; **Logistics relocates to industrial corridors** and IT to **business parks + town centres**. - **Policy insight:** - **F&B:** island-wide, population-following growth → watch **malls/transport nodes**.\ - **IT:** concentrates in **CBD + parks** → plan **flexible office stock** near transit.\ - **Logistics:** anchored to **port/airport/expressways** → reserve **industrial land** and manage **last-mile interfaces** with residential areas. ### Choropleth:counts By Planning Area and Subzone ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #Planning Area counts pa_counts <- biz_pts_use |> st_drop_geometry() |> count(PLN_AREA_N, sector, name = "n") subzones_pa <- subzones_use |> distinct(PLN_AREA_N, .keep_all = TRUE) |> left_join(pa_counts |> group_by(PLN_AREA_N) |> summarise(n_all = sum(n), .groups = "drop"), by = "PLN_AREA_N") # Build a single Singapore outline from your filtered subzones sg_outline <- subzones_use |> st_union() |> # dissolve to one geometry st_make_valid() |> st_as_sf() |> mutate(name = "Singapore") # (dummy column just to keep an sf) tmap_mode("plot") tm_shape(subzones_pa) + tm_polygons( col = "n_all", title = "Registrations (all sectors)", style = "quantile", n = 5, border.col = "grey30", border.lwd = 0.6 ) + tm_shape(sg_outline) + tm_borders(col = "black", lwd = 1.2) + # This baseline choropleth provides the starting point for intensity (KDE) and clustering (K/CSR) analyses in subsequent sections. ## 1st Order Spatio Temporal Analysis Convert sf → owin and ppp ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Build polygonal window (country outline) from filtered subzones W <- spatstat.geom::as.owin(st_union(subzones_use)) # SVY21 metres (EPSG:3414) # Helper: convert an sf points subset to ppp in window W to_ppp <- function(pts_sf) { xy <- sf::st_coordinates(pts_sf) spatstat.geom::ppp(x = xy[,1], y = xy[,2], window = W, check = FALSE) } ``` ::: ### Clark–Evans test per sector The Clark–Evans nearest-neighbour test evaluates whether business registrations are **randomly distributed**, **clustered**, or **regularly spaced** relative to Complete Spatial Randomness (CSR). - **Null hypothesis (H₀):** The point pattern of business registrations follows **CSR** (i.e., randomly distributed).\ - **Alternative hypothesis (H₁):** The point pattern is **more clustered than CSR** (R \< 1). To address this, we employ second-order spatio-temporal analysis (Ripley’s K/L, pair correlation, Knox test, and space–time K-function). These methods allow us to quantify the scales at which new firms tend to emerge together, and whether such patterns differ across sectors (F&B, IT, Logistics). By identifying these interaction ranges, we can link firm behaviour to urban form, infrastructure readiness, and zoning policy — providing actionable spatial intelligence for planners. ### Singapore-wide second-order space–time tests Parameters and Functions for Spatio-Temporal (ST) Point Pattern Analysis This helper block sets up the **parameters and functions** needed for spatio-temporal (ST) point pattern analysis. - **Time window:** Defines the period of study: from **1 Jan 2024 (`t0`) to 30 Jun 2025 (`t1`)**. All business registrations outside this range will be excluded from the analysis. - **Study boundary:** Unions all planning subzones into one boundary polygon (`sg_union`), then converts it into a simple `(x,y)` coordinate matrix `bdry`. This format is required by `splancs::stkhat()` for ST K-function computation. - **Point conversion function (`as_xyz`):** Converts an `sf` point layer into a numeric matrix with three columns: - `x, y`: planar coordinates (SVY21 metres), - `t`: registration time, expressed as days since `t0`. It ensures only points with registration dates inside the study window are included, and matches them by unique ID (`uen`) to keep attributes and geometry aligned. - **Grid definitions:** - `r_vals`: spatial distance lags (metres) for the ST K-function, finer at short ranges (50 m steps up to 500 m) and coarser at larger ranges (up to 4 km). - `u_vals`: temporal lags (days) ranging from 1 week to ~6 months. - **Simulation settings:** - `nsim = 199`: number of Monte Carlo simulations (199 for drafting, increase to 999 for final results). - `set.seed(626)`: ensures reproducibility of simulations. - Creates a cache directory `data/rds` to store results. - **Sectors:** Declares the three business sectors for analysis: **F&B (56), IT (62), and Logistics/Warehousing (52).** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Study window & time bounds (already used earlier) t0 <- as.Date("2024-01-01"); t1 <- as.Date("2025-06-30") # Outer boundary as polygon matrix for splancs::stkhat sg_union <- sf::st_as_sf(sf::st_make_valid(sf::st_union(subzones_use))) bdry <- sf::st_coordinates(sg_union)[,1:2]; colnames(bdry) <- c("x","y") # Convert sf points to [x,y,t] matrix (t=days since t0) as_xyz <- function(sf_pts) { d <- sf::st_drop_geometry(sf_pts) %>% filter(reg_date >= t0, reg_date <= t1) xy <- sf::st_coordinates(sf_pts) # keep only rows that have dates within window xy <- xy[match(d$uen, sf::st_drop_geometry(sf_pts)$uen), , drop = FALSE] cbind(x = xy[,1], y = xy[,2], t = as.numeric(d$reg_date - t0)) } # Grids (SVY21 metres; days) r_vals <- c(seq(0, 500, 50), seq(600, 2000, 200), seq(2500, 4000, 500)) u_vals <- c(7, 14, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180) nsim <- 199 # use 199 for speed while drafting; 999 for final set.seed(626) dir.create("data/rds", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE) sectors <- c("F&B (56)", "IT (62)", "Logistics/Warehousing (52)") ``` ::: Fast Mode Helper Block This is a **“fast mode” helper block** designed to let us run spatio-temporal K-function checks quickly without the full computational cost. - **Chunk options:** - `eval: false` → the code won’t run when knitting (you can toggle it on manually). - `include: false` → the code won’t appear in the rendered document (kept as a hidden utility). - **Simplified grids:** - `r_vals <- seq(0, 1500, by = 250)` → defines a coarse set of 7 **spatial distances** (0, 250, …, 1500 metres). - `u_vals <- c(14, 30, 90)` → defines only 3 **temporal lags**: 2 weeks, 1 month, and 3 months. - **Reduced simulations:** - `nsim <- 19` → runs just 19 Monte Carlo simulations (vs. 199 or 999 in the main analysis). - This makes it **much faster**, but less robust statistically. - **Reproducibility:** - `set.seed(626)` ensures the quick test results are repeatable. Make a clean boundary (fixes NA rows / ensures closed ring) We create a clean boundary matrix for use with `splancs::stkhat()`: - **Function (`make_bdry_mat`):** - Unify polygons in `sf_poly`, validate with `st_make_valid()`. - Keep the **largest polygon** only (avoid offshore islands/artefacts). - Extract `(x,y)` coordinates, drop ring IDs, remove `NA` rows. - Ensure polygon is closed (append first coordinate if needed). - Convert to numeric matrix (`double`), required by `splancs`. - **Sanity check:** - Run `make_bdry_mat(subzones_use)` to generate Singapore boundary. - Confirm output is a 2-column matrix with no `NA` values. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} make_bdry_mat <- function(sf_poly){ u <- sf::st_make_valid(sf::st_union(sf_poly)) pg <- sf::st_cast(u, "POLYGON") pg <- pg[which.max(sf::st_area(pg))] # largest polygon xy <- sf::st_coordinates(pg)[,1:2] # drop ring cols xy <- xy[stats::complete.cases(xy), , drop = FALSE] # remove NA separators if (!all(xy[1,] == xy[nrow(xy),])) xy <- rbind(xy, xy[1,]) # close ring bd <- as.matrix(xy) storage.mode(bd) <- "double" # <- crucial for splancs bd } bdry <- make_bdry_mat(subzones_use) # quick sanity stopifnot(is.matrix(bdry), ncol(bdry) == 2, !any(is.na(bdry))) ``` ::: Safer (x,y,t) converter (keeps rows aligned) This helper converts filtered sf points into a (x, y, t) matrix, where t is days since t0, stored in double precision for compatibility with splancs. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} as_xyz <- function(sf_pts) { sf_use <- dplyr::filter(sf_pts, reg_date >= t0, reg_date <= t1) xy <- sf::st_coordinates(sf_use) X <- cbind(x = xy[,1], y = xy[,2], t = as.numeric(sf_use$reg_date - t0)) storage.mode(X) <- "double" # <- crucial for splancs X } ``` ::: Normalizing `stkhat()` Output with `fix_dims()` We define `fix_dims()` to reshape results from `splancs::stkhat()` into a consistent `ns × nu` matrix: - If a **list** → `unlist()` and reshape to `ns × nu`. - If a **vector** → - `length == ns*nu`: reshape directly. - `length == ns` or `nu`: stop with clear error. - Else: try `as.matrix(K)` and adjust: - If already `ns × nu`, use. - If `nu × ns`, transpose. - Otherwise, throw informative error. - Force **double precision** (`storage.mode(M) <- "double"`) for compatibility. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fix_dims <- function(K, ns, nu){ # splancs::stkhat() can return: # - a matrix (ns x nu), or # - a list (often length ns, each element length nu), or # - a vector (ns*nu) if (is.list(K)) { v <- unlist(K, use.names = FALSE) # flatten list to numeric M <- matrix(v, nrow = ns, ncol = nu, byrow = TRUE) } else { v <- as.numeric(K) if (length(v) == ns * nu) { M <- matrix(v, nrow = ns, ncol = nu) } else if (length(v) == ns || length(v) == nu) { stop("stkhat() returned a length-", length(v), " vector; expected ns*nu = ", ns*nu, ".") } else { # try to coerce if it's a 2D object with swapped dims M0 <- try(as.matrix(K), silent = TRUE) if (inherits(M0, "try-error")) { stop("stkhat() returned unexpected type/shape.") } if (all(dim(M0) == c(ns, nu))) { M <- M0 } else if (all(dim(M0) == c(nu, ns))) { M <- t(M0) } else { stop("stkhat() returned matrix with dims ", paste(dim(M0), collapse="x"), " but expected ", ns, "x", nu, ".") } } } storage.mode(M) <- "double" M } ``` ::: Run space–time K with time-permutation envelopes (all sectors) Spatio-Temporal K-Function Envelopes with Monte Carlo Simulations This chunk defines a workflow to compute **spatio-temporal K-function envelopes** for all business sectors in Singapore, using Monte Carlo simulations. Function `compute_st_env()` - **Inputs:** - `X_xyz`: point events as an `n × 3` matrix (`x, y, t` in double precision). - `s_vals`: vector of spatial distances (metres). - `u_vals`: vector of temporal lags (days). - `poly`: study boundary polygon matrix. - `nsim`: number of random permutations for simulation. - **Observed K-function:** Calls `splancs::stkhat()` to compute the observed spatio-temporal K-function (`K_obs_raw`), then normalizes its shape with `fix_dims()` into an `ns × nu` matrix. - **Null model (permutation test):** - A helper `perm_once()` shuffles the time values while keeping spatial locations fixed. - This simulates the null hypothesis: *no space-time interaction*. - Each shuffled dataset is passed to `stkhat()` and reshaped with `fix_dims()`. - **Monte Carlo simulations:** Repeats the permutation `nsim` times, storing results in a 3D array (`ns × nu × nsim`). - **Envelopes:** For each spatial–temporal grid cell, calculates: - `lo`: 2.5% quantile (lower bound), - `hi`: 97.5% quantile (upper bound), - `med`: median across simulations. - **Output:** Returns a list with observed K, envelope bounds, median, and the `s` and `u` grids. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # pts: matrix [n x 3] with cols x,y,t (all doubles) compute_st_env <- function(X_xyz, s_vals, u_vals, poly, nsim = 99) { xy <- X_xyz[, 1:2, drop = FALSE] times <- as.double(X_xyz[, 3]) tlim <- range(times, finite = TRUE) ns <- length(s_vals); nu <- length(u_vals) # observed K_obs_raw <- splancs::stkhat(pts = xy, times = times, s = s_vals, tm = u_vals, poly = poly, tlim = tlim) K_obs <- fix_dims(K_obs_raw, ns, nu) # permutation null: shuffle times only perm_once <- function(){ tp <- sample(times, replace = FALSE) Kp <- splancs::stkhat(pts = xy, times = tp, s = s_vals, tm = u_vals, poly = poly, tlim = tlim) fix_dims(Kp, ns, nu) } K_sim <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(ns, nu, nsim)) for (i in seq_len(nsim)) K_sim[,,i] <- perm_once() lo <- apply(K_sim, c(1,2), quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE) hi <- apply(K_sim, c(1,2), quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE) med <- apply(K_sim, c(1,2), median, na.rm = TRUE) list(K_obs = K_obs, K_lo = lo, K_hi = hi, K_med = med, s = s_vals, u = u_vals) } st_sg <- list() for (sec in sectors) { pts <- dplyr::filter(biz_pts_use, sector == sec, reg_date >= t0, reg_date <= t1) xyz <- as_xyz(pts) if (nrow(xyz) < 30) { message("Skipping sparse: ", sec); next } cache_name <- paste0("stk_env_SG_", gsub("\\W","_",sec), "_ns", length(r_vals), "_nu", length(u_vals), "_nsim", nsim, ".rds") rds <- file.path("data/rds", cache_name) force_recompute <- TRUE # <- set TRUE now st_sg[[sec]] <- if (!force_recompute && file.exists(rds)) { readRDS(rds) } else { res <- compute_st_env(xyz, r_vals, u_vals, bdry, nsim = nsim) saveRDS(res, rds); res } } ``` ::: Loading and Standardizing Spatio-Temporal K-Function Results This chunk **loads and standardizes** a previously saved spatio-temporal K-function result: 1. **Load result:** Reads an RDS file containing simulation outputs (`res`). 2. **Rebuild grids:** Reconstructs spatial (`r_vals_fast`) and temporal (`u_vals_fast`) lags based on the filename (`ns7`, `nu3`). Minimal theme. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ggplot2) plot_st_heat_tile <- function(res, title){ ns <- length(res$s); nu <- length(res$u) D <- res$K_obs - res$K_med sig <- (res$K_obs > res$K_hi) - (res$K_obs < res$K_lo) df <- expand.grid(ir = seq_len(ns), iu = seq_len(nu)) df$r <- res$s[df$ir] df$u <- res$u[df$iu] df$excess <- as.vector(D) df$sig <- as.vector(sig) df$is_na <- !is.finite(df$excess) # cell width/height from grid spacing (robust) dr <- diff(sort(unique(res$s))); w <- if (length(dr)) median(dr) else 1 du <- diff(sort(unique(res$u))); h <- if (length(du)) median(du) else 1 ggplot() + # draw NA tiles first so the row/column is visible geom_tile( data = subset(df, is_na), aes(r, u), width = w, height = h, fill = "grey95", color = NA ) + # draw finite tiles with colour scale geom_tile( data = subset(df, !is_na), aes(r, u, fill = excess), width = w, height = h, color = NA ) + # significance markers (✳ = above band, × = below) geom_point( data = subset(df, sig != 0 & !is_na), aes(r, u, shape = factor(sig)), size = 2, color = "black" ) + scale_shape_manual(values = c("-1" = 4, "1" = 8), guide = "none") + scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C") + scale_x_continuous(breaks = res$s, expand = c(0,0)) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = res$u, expand = c(0,0)) + labs(x = "Space lag r (m)", y = "Time lag u (days)", fill = "K_obs − median", title = title) + theme_minimal() + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # (Optional in your qmd chunk) #| fig.width: 7 # #| fig.height: 4 print(plot_st_heat_tile(res, "F&B (56) — ST-K excess")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Take_Home_Ex01_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-27-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: F&B (SSIC 56) – Space–time K excess (Jan 2024–Jun 2025) Heat map shows \(K_{\text{obs}}\) – median under a time-permutation null (spatial pattern held fixed). - **Blue cells** indicate values near expectation; - **Yellow cells** indicate excess pairs.
